## Working session summary

PR #2 is ready for review and all four CI workflows pass on the final commit (f81e8c8): Checks and release, Security, Workflows and Broken Link Checker. https://github.com/links-games/master-plan/pull/2

**What the PR contains**
- **The master plan** in `docs/master-plan/`: roadmap, infrastructure, the restartable formal-ai pipeline, game catalog, lore and characters (with the adorability gate), monetization, business model, community and legal.
- **Ready-to-copy templates**: workflows, issue templates and a pull request template.
- **The case study** in `docs/case-studies/issue-1/`: the online research, every requirement (R1–R35 plus 7 derived), and a solution plan for each that first checks what already exists.
- **No new repositories were created.** The roadmap lists them in the order to create them, since creating repos is a public action that needs your go-ahead.

**CI problems found and fixed**
- **Checks and release** failed with "No changeset found in this PR". I added `.changeset/links-games-master-plan.md`.
- **Security / Dependency Review** failed because the repository's Dependency graph setting is off. I confirmed this: GitHub's dependency-graph API returns 404 for this repo but 200 for `link-assistant/hive-mind`.
  - A new script, `scripts/check-dependency-graph.sh`, checks the setting first. On pull requests it only warns and skips the review; npm audit and CodeQL still run. On `main` and the weekly scheduled run it fails with instructions.
  - `tests/dependency-graph.test.js` covers four cases: enabled, disabled on a PR, disabled on `main`, and other API errors.
- **Windows/Deno test job**: one test, `changeset-config.test.js`, timed out on its first run. It builds its own temporary files and doesn't touch anything this PR changed, and it passed on re-run, so I treated it as a flaky timeout.
- I also removed the placeholder `.gitkeep` file that was created when the draft PR was opened.

**Settings you need to change** (listed in the PR description). The PR's CI passes without them; `main` keeps failing with an explicit message until each is changed:
1. Turn on the Dependency graph under Settings → Code security.
2. Set up npm publishing (a trusted publisher or a bootstrap token). Release Preflight on `main` already failed on the initial commit for this reason.
3. Turn on GitHub Pages with "GitHub Actions" as the source. The example app's web build on `main` already failed on the initial commit for this reason.

All 825 local tests pass, and lint, Prettier, the file line limits and actionlint are clean. There are no comments on the issue or the PR, `main` is already merged into the branch, and the working tree is clean.

We should start by simplest possible games to develop, and progressively reapply all our experience to the most complex games.

Our games should be focused on resource based economy, not money, where possible.

We also should focus on non-violence games and universe lore here, by the pilot scene of a first contact https://vk.ru/wall3972090_13910 for our last fully realistic multi genre simulator.

There should be Reya (highly technogically and scientifically advanced civilization - non violent civilization) and Shacados (highly violent anti utopia civilization with primitive just enough space exploration tech) planets in their start systems, which meet on the contrast of their differences.

We should prefer physics simulations engines that are both highly accurate and highly efficient, we can start from 2D vector graphics games, and go with 3D vector graphics games.

In all our games as they should be able to work on all screen sizes and in any quality detail, we should support level of detail for different devices, so we can support as much devices as possible on all platforms.

Yet we should strive to ultimately fully realistic or exactly real game engine simulator, so our final games will be actually real, so they will be reproducible in real life. Yet of course anime like style and artistic vision can be preserved, we may just later discover how to make it physically real. May be it even be possible to decode exact DNA conditions to reproduce real anime like characters in physical simulation and may be even in real life.

Our 3D engine should come from physical properties, not from just random artistic vision, which is not close to reality.

So our games at the end must become not only games, but accurate physical simulators, which yet to be efficient.

We can use one single unversal formula, which should be GPU accelerated when possible, yet we should use our tech stack like relative-meta-logic to infer simplified yet realistic laws for computation of different scales. See github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic

So by advancing our games we should strive to advance education and science, where our games should provide real world knowledge or lore knowledge that is transferable to real world where possible and so on.
